finding: #99 bounded columnar write memory (incremental stripe flush)
verdict: 64x more rows -> ~46.0x more stripes (LINEAR in N) while the peak pending set stays ~constant (~maintenance_work_mem): 2148.44 KB at 50k vs 2989.13 KB at 3.2M rows. Write memory is O(maintenance_work_mem), NOT O(rows-in-xact). Before M104 an INSERT of N rows buffered all N and produced ONE stripe; now it produces N/(mwm/rowbytes) stripes and the pending set never exceeds mwm. #99 closed.
honest_note: The DETERMINISTIC signal is stripe-count linearity + a ~constant per-stripe pending bound (peak pending = total_bytes / n_stripes ~ mwm). A /proc VmHWM sample was attempted but is dominated by the shared-lib/planner baseline, so it is not reported as the primary evidence; the stripe-linearity is the honest bounded-memory proof (a single-stripe O(N) buffer would show stripes=1 at every N).
